change: Add a private IPv4 return-address lease per existing endpoint from the same node pool, stored separately from configured Pod addresses. Allocation is idempotent and durable; endpoint release persists both lease tables together and restores both on failure.

storage.formats1And2: Existing single/dual-family shapes remain in use without private leases.
storage.format3: Ordered CIDRs and Pod address arrays plus serviceSNATAllocations keyed by sandboxID/interfaceName with one IPv4 address. Older formats carrying that field are rejected rather than ignoring live leases.
storage.validation: Reject unknown/duplicate owners, duplicate numeric addresses across both tables, network/broadcast/out-of-pool/noncanonical alias addresses, and malformed arrays. Validate both tables before hot reload replaces either.
storage.ownership: A canonical address identity is used for free-space search across Pod and private leases; valid legacy stored address text is preserved. IPv6-only pools cannot allocate IPv4 aliases.

validation.coverage: All Service/networking/egress-guard/NetworkPolicy suites and all99 CNI/node-session/IPAM tests. Includes ordinary and dual-stack restart, private lease exclusion from Pod address lists, idempotency, release/reuse, allocation and joint-release rollback, exhaustion, malformed/duplicate/orphan state, atomic invalid hot reload, legacy spellings and IPv6-only refusal.

scope: Allocation prerequisite only. No CNI caller or packet rewrite uses these leases yet. Runtime return-route installation, trusted alias identity distribution, endpoint generation fencing, source NAT, direct-flow/Service collision ownership, policy normalization, versioned packet maps/GC/upgrades and actual guest/native TCP/UDP hairpin/collision tests remain required under podster-p9c.10. Parent also retains IPv6 packet NAT, packet NodePort and broader Service semantics/diagnostics work.
